name: Bernd Lange - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the non-application of customs duties on imports of certain goods
part_text:
The report sets Parliament's position on a law that removes European import duties on American lobster, both live and frozen and now also processed. The old duty-free deal expired on 31 July 2025, so the new law would apply from that date until 31 December 2028. It also lets the Commission switch the duties back on if the United States raises its own tariffs on European goods above 15 percent or breaches democratic and security principles.

- What changes: no import duties on American lobster until the end of 2028, with a possible early switch back on.
- Who it affects: European importers and sellers of lobster, and the European Union budget, which gives up about 7.5 million euros a year.
- What happens next: Parliament votes on this position, then negotiates the final text with European Union governments.
